cells.verb: keeping a small practice lit by attention
cells.place: in the clearing where something has ended
cells.ask: Offer one finished thing to be let go — and when you do, watch what arrives to replace it, because a real ending is what lets a real beginning land.
cells.core:
You keep a small practice going — the same few minutes, the same few moves, repeated — and it's not forced. The quiet is where you're most connected to people, not where you hide from them; the refining sharpens what you're building instead of feeding a worry. That's a rare thing to have running, and it's running because you keep lighting it.

A clearing has already happened around you — something ended — and rather than scattering, you went small and steady. The steadiness is doing what the ending opened space for.
cells.sheetLine: Your practice is quiet, and it connects you instead of cutting you off — an ending made room, and you filled it with attention.

cells.verb: refining past the point where refining helps
cells.place: guarding a clearing that isn't finished happening
cells.ask: Let one thing end before you're certain it's safe — and notice that releasing flows from finishing, not from defeat. When you let it go, space opens where you were gripping.
cells.core:
You're ahead of yourself, bracing for what happens if you stop. The practice has turned into polishing, and the polishing has turned into a guard — solitude stops being chosen and starts feeling necessary, and you keep going not because the work asks but because stopping has become the thing to fear. What was a small steady light has become a watch you can't put down.

Every version gets held up and tightened, and the tightening is spending the same attention the practice was built to gather. The bracing is costing you the thing you're bracing to protect.
cells.sheetLine: You've turned your practice into a guard — refining so nothing has to end, when something needs to end.

cells.tense: past tense, still at a door that's behind you
cells.place: standing outside a clearing that's already happened
cells.ask: Take one fair step with someone — give what's theirs and receive what's yours without calculating — and let that exchange pull a little steadiness back through. When the balance returns, practice stops feeling dangerous and starts feeling like yours again.
cells.core:
You haven't been able to keep anything going long enough to feel like yours. Somewhere back there practicing cost you something, and you're still listening to that — so the repeating never gets to build, and you stay outside the clearing where the ending already happened. It isn't that you lack the wanting. It's that the wanting learned to stay quiet.

The door you're avoiding is behind you, not ahead. The practice you're waiting to feel safe enough to start is the one that was interrupted, not one you're failing at now.
cells.sheetLine: You've stopped letting practice build — standing outside a clearing that already happened, waiting to feel safe first.

cells.tense: disowned present, pen down in a room you're already writing
cells.verb: already practicing, while calling it something else
cells.place: in a clearing you don't remember making
cells.ask: Name one thing you've been doing as practice and stop calling it luck or instinct — then let the ambiguity stay unresolved a while. When you do, real vision comes from everything you've already processed, not from forcing the answer.
cells.core:
You're already doing the work — the repeated moves, the small steady attention, the refining — and you talk about it like it happens on its own. Expertise shows up, and you credit instinct or luck. The practice is running; the claim on it isn't.

The clearing around you is real, and you didn't experience yourself making it. Something ended, you kept going, and the steadiness that carried you through doesn't get counted as yours.
cells.sheetLine: You're already practicing — it's running under the name instinct, and you never said it was yours.
